_about: Order 139 part 2 (docs/order-139-part2-spec.md): the CRS grouping and order cases BOTH sides must pass. Backend: crs_mapping.crs_groups over each case's findings (base_finding with the case's finding laid over it; a null overrides) must give exactly `expected_rows`, in order: each row's finding ids (compared as a SET - the leader is the server's), its priority and word, its action line (null on a row of one clause) and its clause count (distinct standard_document_id + standard_clause). Every id in `not_on_sheet` is in no row. Frontend: crs/crsGroups.parity.test.ts turns `expected_rows` into the run summary's per-finding fields (crs_group = 'row-<index>', crs_order = index, crs_priority, crs_priority_label, crs_action) and buildCrsRows must show one row per expected row, with exactly those findings, in that order, and none of `not_on_sheet` in a grouped row. `review_notes` (absent = none): the findings the file lists in its Review notes instead of on a row - the summary marks them `crs_note`, and the screen shows them as a note, never as a row to decide. The fields under base_finding are the ones the server's grouping reads after comparison.attach_crs_context (crs_field_label, requirement_limit). Invented data only - no client document, no real standard text.
